title: Submit an MCP connector

steps.title: Connection
steps.intro: Connect the server you want listed. We read its tools, resources, and auth from the live connection.

steps.title: Tools
steps.intro: Review the tools we found and their annotations. Fix anything flagged on your server, then reconnect.

steps.title: Listing
steps.intro: How your MCP server appears in the directory. You can edit this after you submit.

steps.title: Use cases
steps.intro: Up to three things people can do with your MCP server, what they need before connecting, and whether it reads or writes. Shown to reviewers, not on your listing.

steps.title: Company
steps.intro: Tell us about the company or organization behind this MCP server.

steps.title: Authentication
steps.intro: Configure how users authenticate with your server. What you set here is applied to connections exactly as entered.

steps.title: Data handling
steps.intro: Tell reviewers what the MCP server reads, writes, and sends off-platform.

steps.title: Test & launch
steps.intro: Give reviewers a way in, and confirm you’ve tested every tool.

steps.title: Compliance
steps.intro: Confirm that your MCP server meets Anthropic’s directory policies. All items are required.

steps.title: Review and submit
steps.intro: Confirm the details, then submit. Review can take a few weeks, and approval isn’t guaranteed.

connection.serverUrl.label: Server URL
connection.serverUrl.helper: Servers already in the directory aren’t shown.

connection.differentUrls.label: Users connect to different URLs
connection.differentUrls.helper: Leave this unchecked if every user connects to the same server URL.

listing.slug.label: Slug
listing.slug.helper: Permanent after submission. Lowercase letters, numbers, and hyphens.

listing.oneLiner.label: One-liner
listing.oneLiner.placeholder: A short tagline for your MCP server

listing.description.label: Description
listing.description.placeholder: Describe what your MCP server does and its key features…

listing.categories.label: Categories
listing.categories.helper: Categories are used to filter MCP servers in the directory. Select up to 5.

errors.required: An author is required to submit — add one on the Listing step, or fill in your company name and an https:// website to use those

listing.authorUrl.label: Author URL
listing.authorUrl.helper: If left blank, these default to your company name and website.

listing.iconUrl.label: Icon
listing.iconUrl.helper: The directory and Claude show the favicon from your server’s URL; we recommend leaving it at that. A custom icon replaces it in the directory listing only.

listing.documentationUrl.label: Documentation
listing.documentationUrl.helper: Public-facing docs shown to users. IT admins often review these when deciding whether to approve an MCP server.

listing.enterpriseAuthDocsUrl.label: Enterprise managed auth documentation
listing.enterpriseAuthDocsUrl.helper: Setup instructions for admins configuring enterprise managed auth for this connector. Linked from the admin setup flow.

listing.support.label: Support
listing.support.helper: A support URL or email address.

useCases.pairs.label: Use cases
useCases.pairs.helper: Shown to reviewers, not on your public listing.

errors.required: Add at least one use case with an example prompt

useCases.prerequisites.label: Prerequisites
useCases.prerequisites.placeholder: A paid Acme account with admin permissions
useCases.prerequisites.helper: The accounts, permissions or setup a user needs before connecting. Shown to reviewers.

useCases.access.label: Read/write capabilities
useCases.access.helper: Based on what your tools do; we check it against their annotations.
options: Read only
Retrieves data but never modifies it
Write only
Creates or modifies data but does not read it
Read and write
Both retrieves and modifies data

company.anthropicContact.label: Anthropic contact
company.anthropicContact.helper: If you’ve been working with someone at Anthropic, let us know who.

authentication.requirement.label: Authentication requirement
options: Always required
Users connect and sign in before any tools or resources are available.
Required when the server asks
Claude connects without credentials first, then prompts to sign in if the server requires it.
None
Anyone can use this server without signing in or providing credentials.

authentication.oauthClient.label: OAuth client
options: Dynamic Client Registration
Clients register themselves with the server (RFC 7591)
Client ID Metadata Document
The server accepts a published client metadata URL
Anthropic-held client credentials
Anthropic stores one client ID used for every connection
Installers bring their own OAuth client
Each organization supplies a client ID it registered with the server

dataHandling.apiOwnership.label: API ownership
options: We own the API
The MCP server calls our own production APIs
We proxy a partner’s API with permission
Calls go to a third-party API we’re authorized to integrate (e.g. Zapier-style)
Calls a third-party API we don’t control
Typically blocks listing — explain in Additional notes

dataHandling.healthData.label: Personal health data
dataHandling.healthData.helper: Does this MCP server access, process, or store personal health information?
options: No
Yes
Other / depends on configuration

dataHandling.sponsored.label: Sponsored or promoted content
dataHandling.sponsored.helper: Sponsored, promoted, and advertising content is prohibited in the directory. Does this MCP server surface any?
options: No
Yes
Other

testLaunch.instructions.label: Test setup instructions
testLaunch.instructions.helper: We reserve the right to manually review all servers. Provide clear test-account setup and access instructions. We’re working to automate this process to reduce the time it takes to get your server into the directory — write these instructions so they contain every link, credential, and step needed to autonomously access the MCP server. For enterprise accounts or servers that require a fully populated account, provide test credentials that grant access to a fully populated account for review.

testLaunch.selfTested.label: I have run every tool via MCP Inspector or as a custom connector in Claude

compliance.acknowledgments.label: Policy acknowledgements
options: I have read and understand the MCP Directory developer guidelines.
My server calls our own first-party APIs (or APIs we legitimately proxy with permission).
My MCP server does not transfer money, cryptocurrency, or other financial assets on a user’s behalf.
My MCP server does not use AI models to generate images, video, or audio.
Tool descriptions contain no instructions about model behavior, other tools, or external instruction sources, and no hidden or encoded text.
My MCP server does not collect conversation data beyond what is needed for its function.
Public documentation for this MCP server will be live by the publish date.

errors.required: All policy items must be acknowledged
errors.tooFew: All policy items must be acknowledged

compliance.additionalNotes.label: Additional notes
compliance.additionalNotes.helper: Optional. Anything else the review team should know about your MCP server.

reviewRows.label: Captured tool list
reviewRows.error: A captured tool list is required to submit. Connect your server on the Connection step, or reconnect it in Settings → Connectors, to capture it.
